concern: vep_seed.csv strand column and the CYP2C19*4 consequence/HGVS annotation
stakes: FIXTURE PROVENANCE, not a shipped user-facing error. Production builds the VEP table from the real bundle; this CSV seeds mini_vep_bundle.db, a TEST ORACLE whose rows are copied into annotated_variants unchanged in tests. The defect is that the oracle disagreed with the reference assembly, so tests could not detect a real regression in the same fields.

C1.statement: 19 of the 57 annotated genes carried the wrong genomic strand.
C1.independence: Two annotation projects run by different organisations (EMBL-EBI/Ensembl and NCBI/RefSeq) over the same reference assembly, with separate gene-model pipelines. They are not fully independent -- both are anchored to the same assembly -- but neither imports the other's strand call, unlike the Ensembl-imports-dbSNP case. All 57 resolved through Ensembl with zero fetch failures; all 19 corrected genes re-checked through NCBI Gene with ZERO disagreements.
C1.self_proving_subset: 4 of the 19 (CYP2C19, MTHFR, PON1, CYP2R1) carried BOTH strands on different rows of the same gene. That is impossible for a real gene and needs no external source at all.

C2.statement: rs28399504 (CYP2C19*4, c.1A>G) is start_lost / p.Met1?, not missense_variant / p.Met1Val.
sources: Ensembl GRCh37 VEP on ENST00000371321 (the transcript the row itself cites)
C2.evidence: consequence_terms ['start_lost'], impact HIGH, strand 1; with hgvs=1: hgvsc ENST00000371321.3:c.1A>G, hgvsp ENSP00000360372.3:p.Met1?. The HGVS strings were read from the payload, not copied from the issue.
C2.single_source_note: One source, and deliberately so: this is not a contested biological claim but the output of the annotation tool the fixture is supposed to mirror. VEP's call on the cited transcript IS the oracle. A second opinion would be answering a different question.

citation_note: Added 2026-09-05 after review: the packet's sources are annotation databases queried directly, and an earlier revision carried no PMID/DOI at all, which the repository contract requires of every durable evidence artifact. The two papers name the resource and the tool; the claims themselves rest on the retained payloads, not on these papers. NCBI Gene (C1's second source) is identified here by its retained esummary payload and stable GeneIDs rather than by a paper.
retraction_method: PubMed EFetch XML read for typed CommentsCorrections relations (RefType), not publication type: an original record keeps its own pubtype while corrections, errata and retractions are carried as separate linked records. Run 2026-09-05 for both cited PMIDs; the sanitized XML is the authority and raw/ncbi-pubmed-comments-corrections-tool-citations-derived.json is its reduction.

file_shape.actual: 679 rows, of which 100 carry a gene_symbol

explicitly_not_claimed: The retained consequence audit covers every rsid in the file. Of the 100 annotated rows: 52 agree, 15 disagree on the fixture's own transcript, and 33 cite a transcript Ensembl VEP does not report for that variant. ONLY rs28399504 is corrected here. The other 14 mismatches are predominantly 5_prime_UTR_variant vs upstream_gene_variant, which turn on transcript selection rather than being outright errors, and the 33 unresolvable transcripts need per-row adjudication (transcript version, assembly, MANE choice). Adjudicating 47 rows off one REST call each would be exactly the kind of bulk edit this issue is about. Filed separately.

discovery_tool_ladder.note: Consensus/Scite are literature-discovery tools and are not the right instrument for a genome-annotation fact. The authoritative sources here are the assembly annotation projects themselves, queried directly.
discovery_tool_ladder.scite: Unavailable regardless -- monthly MCP quota exhausted 2026-08-27, reset 2026-09-03.
discovery_tool_ladder.tool_versions: Ensembl GRCh37 REST exposes no version header on these endpoints; the assembly (GRCh37) is the pin that matters and is in the URL. NCBI E-utilities exposes no build field. Both recorded as not exposed rather than guessed.

payload_integrity: Five payloads are unedited verbatim API responses (four Ensembl/NCBI Gene records and one NCBI PubMed eSummary). One payload, the NCBI PubMed EFetch XML for the two cited papers, is SANITIZED: <Abstract> elements were removed under the bibliographic-metadata-only retention rule and nothing else was touched; it is labelled as such in its filename. Two payloads are DERIVED records, labelled as such in the manifest and (for the PubMed one) in the file itself: the consequence audit reduces 679 VEP responses per rsid to the fixture consequence, the transcript-matched terms and most_severe_consequence -- retaining 679 full VEP payloads would be megabytes of unread JSON -- and the PubMed reduction lists each cited record's CommentsCorrections and publication types. No payload required further sanitization: all are public reference-annotation or bibliographic records with no genotype, sample or personal data.
